name: Envy

counsel.text: Ask envy what it would have; -- murder and destruction is at the end of it. Set thyself against it with no less vigour than if it had utterly debased thee to wickedness. Without this course thou wilt not prevail.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: We aim at God's glory when we are content to be outshined by others in gifts and esteem, so that his glory may be increased. A man that has God in his heart, and God's glory in his eye, desires that God should be exalted; and if this be effected, let who will be the instrument, he rejoices.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: A Body of Divinity, man's chief end

counsel.text: The second cause of discontent is, envy, which Augustine calls the sin of the devil. Satan envied Adam the glory of paradise, and the robe of innocency: he that envies what his neighbour hath, is never contented with that portion which God's providence doth parcel out to him.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 11

counsel.text: If men are poor, they learn to be envious; they malign those that are above them. Another's prosperity is an eye-sore. When God's candle shines upon their neighbour's tabernacle, this light offends them.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 9

counsel.text: Envy drinks its own venom. The viper, which leaped on Paul's hand, thought to have hurt Paul, but fell into the fire itself. Acts 28: 3. So, while the envious man thinks to hurt another, he destroys himself.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the sixth commandment

counsel.text: Wicked men are the most needy men in the world, yea, they want those two things that should render their mercies sweet, viz., the blessing of God, and content with their condition, and without which their heaven is but hell on this side hell.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: Humility can weep over other men's weaknesses, and joy and rejoice over their graces. Humility will make a man quiet and contented in the meanest condition, and it will preserve a man from envying other men's prosperous condition, 1 Thes. 1. 2, 3. Humility honours those that are strong in grace, and puts two hands under those that are weak in grace, Eph. 3. 8.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks

counsel.text: For our Christian calling, we must know that Christianity is a matter rather of grace than of gifts, of obedience than of parts. Gifts may come from a more common work of the Spirit; they are common to castaways, and are more for others than for ourselves. Grace comes from a peculiar favour of God, and especially for our own good.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 25

counsel.text: 'The spirit that dwelleth in us lusteth to envy,' James 4:5. Our corrupt nature is ever putting on to this sin. It is as hard to keep our hearts and this sin asunder, as it is to keep two lovers from meeting together. Thatch is not more ready to be fired with every flash of lightning, than the heart to be kindled at every shining forth of any excelling gift or grace in another.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: God can give thee more grace than thou hast sin—more humility than thou hast pride. Be but so humble as cordially to beg this grace, and thou shalt not be so proud as wickedly to envy his gifts or grace in others.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: It troubles thee, it seems, that God hath a heart to do good to any besides thyself; thine eye is evil, because he is good. Wouldst not thou have God be good? you might as well say, you would not have him God. He can as soon cease to be God as to be good.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: Thou canst not love and envy the same person. Envy is as contrary to love, as the hectical feverish fire in the body is to the kindly heat of nature. 'Charity envieth not,' 1 Cor. 13:4. How can it, when it lives where it loves?
counsel.author: William Gurnall

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Generous Father, every good and perfect gift comes from you, and you give to each one as you will. I come in the name of your Son. I confess that I have envied. I have looked at the gifts, the success, and the blessings you have given others, and I have resented them. I have been secretly glad at their trouble and sorry at their joy. In my heart I have accused you of being unfair, as if you owed me what you freely gave to them. Envy has made me blind to my own mercies and cold toward my neighbor. It is rebellion against your wise providence, and it is rottenness to the bones. Forgive me, Lord. Christ, who had everything, made himself poor for my sake, so that by his poverty I might become rich. In him you have given me every spiritual blessing, and you have given me yourself. For his sake pardon my envy. Holy Spirit, put it to death, and teach me to rejoice with those who rejoice. Make me content with your portion for me, and glad of your goodness to others. I thank you that you are my portion forever. In Jesus' name. Amen.

prayers.title: When envy stirs
prayers.text: Lord, I see what another has, and something sour is rising in me. I confess it to you now, before it grows. You are good, and you do me no wrong when you are generous to someone else. Turn my eyes from their portion to mine, for you have given me Christ, and with him all things. Help me to thank you for their blessing and to ask for their good, even now. Holy Spirit, root out this envy, and give me a heart that is glad at my neighbor's joy. Amen.

prayers.title: For a glad heart toward others
prayers.text: Father, love does not envy. Fill me with that love. Teach me to see the gifts you give others as gifts to your whole church, and to delight in them. Free me from comparing myself with others, and from measuring my worth by what I have or what I do. Let my worth rest in this, that I am your child through Christ. Give me joy in serving where you have placed me, without needing to be first or seen. Make me quick to praise and slow to compete, so that the good of others makes me thankful and not bitter. For Christ's sake. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing envy and uncharitableness
prayers.text: Contrary to the royal law of charity, we have vaunted ourselves, and been puffed up, have behaved ourselves unseemly, and sought our own, have been easily provoked, have rejoiced in iniquity, and been secretly glad at calamities. We have been desirous of vain-glory, provoking one another, envying one another; when we should have considered one another to provoke to love and to good works.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

prayers.title: That envy may be put to death in us
prayers.text: Mortify in us all envy, hatred, malice, and uncharitableness; pluck up these roots of bitterness out of our minds, and give us grace to love one another with a pure heart fervently, as becomes the followers of the Lord Jesus, who has given us this as his new commandment. O that brotherly love may continue among us, love without dissimulation.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: Whose blessing, gift, or honor stirred something sour in you today, and what did that feeling say about how you think God has dealt with you?
How did envy show itself, in faint praise, quiet criticism, comparing, or a secret gladness when someone stumbled?
What has God given you that you overlooked today because you were looking at what he gave someone else?
Can you rejoice with the one you envy? What would it take to pray for their good by name and mean it?
Have you tried to lift yourself higher by bringing someone else lower, even only in your own thoughts or in what you let others believe about them?
If you have Christ, what is it that you still think you are missing? Is he enough for you?
fleeActions: Pray for the person you envy by name, asking God to bless them in the very thing you resent.
Say something honest and kind about that person to someone else today, or tell them yourself that you are glad for them.
Write down on paper three gifts God has given you this week, and thank him for each one out loud.
Close whatever keeps setting other people's lives before your eyes, and go do the work God has given you for today.
Open your Bible to Psalm 73, read it slowly, and pray verses 25 and 26 back to God in your own words.
Tell a trusted believer in your church that you are fighting envy, and ask them to pray that you would be content in Christ.

afterFallReadings.text: Envy is a sin which breaks both tables at once; it begins in discontent against God, and ends in injury against man, as we see in Cain.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Ten Commandments, the sixth commandment

afterFallReadings.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
